title: Hindi grammar
intro: A working reference for beginners to intermediate learners, in Devanagari with translations. Hindi puts the verb at the end, uses postpositions instead of prepositions, and marks gender on verbs and adjectives: read a section, notice the shape, then listen for it in what you watch and read.

sections.title: Word order (subject, object, verb)
sections.text: The verb comes last: **मैं चाय पीता हूँ** (I tea drink am). Time and place usually come early. A yes/no question starts with **क्या** or simply rises in tone; question words (कौन, क्या, कहाँ, कब, क्यों, कैसे) stay where the answer would be.

examples.text: मैं हर दिन हिंदी पढ़ता हूँ।
कल हम दिल्ली जा रहे हैं।

sections.title: Nouns, gender & plural
sections.text: Every noun is masculine or feminine, and adjectives and verbs agree with it. Most nouns in **-आ** are masculine, most in **-ई** feminine, but learn the gender with each word (पानी, water, is masculine; बात, matter, is feminine). Adjectives in **-आ** change: **अच्छा लड़का, अच्छे लड़के, अच्छी लड़की**; others never change: **सुंदर घर**.

examples.translation: My books are on the table.

sections.title: Pronouns, तू / तुम / आप
sections.text: Choose **आप** with anyone you don't know well; it takes plural verbs even for one person. **तुम** is for friends, **तू** for very close people (and can sound rude to others). **यह/ये** point near, **वह/वे** far; a single person you respect is referred to with the plural **वे**.

examples.text: तुम कल क्या कर रहे हो?
examples.translation: What are you doing tomorrow? (to a friend)

sections.title: Postpositions & the oblique form
sections.text: Postpositions come **after** the noun, and the noun before them takes its **oblique** form: masculine **-आ** becomes **-े** (कमरा → **कमरे में**), plurals end in **-ों** (लड़के → **लड़कों को**, किताबें → **किताबों में**). Pronouns too: मैं → **मुझ**, तुम → **तुम्ह**, वह → **उस**, यह → **इस** (**उससे**, **मुझसे**).

examples.translation: He is sitting in the room.
examples.note: कमरा → कमरे in front of में

examples.text: मैं बच्चों के लिए खाना बना रही हूँ।

sections.title: का / के / की (of), possessives
sections.text: **का** means "of" and agrees with the **thing owned**, not the owner, like an adjective in -आ. The possessive pronouns behave the same way: **मेरा/मेरे/मेरी**, **तुम्हारा**, **आपका**, **उसका**, **हमारा**, **उनका**.

head: Owned thing
का form
Example
rows: राम के दोस्त ;; मेरे घर में

examples.text: मेरे माता-पिता गाँव में रहते हैं।
examples.translation: My parents live in the village.

sections.title: होना (to be): है, था
sections.text: **है** (is) and **था** (was) close most sentences and also build the tenses below. The past agrees in gender: **था** (masculine), **थी** (feminine), **थे** (masculine plural or polite), **थीं** (feminine plural).

sections.title: Present habitual (करता हूँ) & continuous (कर रहा हूँ)
sections.text: Take the stem (करना → **कर**) and add **-ता/-ती/-ते** for things you do regularly, or **रहा/रही/रहे** for what is happening now; **है/हूँ/हैं** comes last. The ending agrees with the subject's gender. With **था** instead of है you get the past: **करता था** (used to do), **कर रहा था** (was doing).

examples.text: हम अभी खाना खा रहे हैं।
बचपन में मैं क्रिकेट खेलता था।
examples.translation: As a child I used to play cricket.

sections.title: Simple past & ने
sections.text: The simple past is stem + **-आ/-ए/-ई/-ईं**. With verbs that take an object (खाना, देखना, करना…), the subject gets **ने** and the verb agrees with the **object** instead: **मैंने रोटी खाई** (roti is feminine → खाई). Without an object, or with को, the verb stays masculine singular: **उसने मुझे देखा**. Verbs without an object (जाना, आना) take no ने and agree with the subject: **वह आई।**

examples.translation: I went to the market yesterday.

sections.title: Future & subjunctive
sections.text: The **subjunctive** (stem + ऊँ/ए/ओ/एँ) expresses wishes, suggestions and possibilities: **चलें?** (shall we go?), **शायद वह आए** (maybe he'll come). Add **-गा/-गी/-गे** to it for the future. **होना** has a short future too: **होगा** also means "must be" (**वह घर पर होगा** – he's probably at home).

sections.title: Imperatives & polite requests
sections.text: Match the request to the pronoun you use with the person. Irregular polite forms: **कीजिए** (करना), **दीजिए** (देना), **लीजिए** (लेना), **पीजिए** (पीना). **ज़रा** softens a request; **मत** makes it negative: **मत जाओ**.

examples.translation: Could you give me some water?

sections.title: मुझे... (to me): likes, needs and feelings
sections.text: Many everyday feelings are said "to someone": the person takes **को** (मुझे = मुझको, तुम्हें, उसे, हमें, आपको), and the thing liked or needed is the grammatical subject. **चाहिए** alone means "should": **आपको आराम करना चाहिए**.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: it seems to me / I feel

examples.text: मुझे हिंदी फ़िल्में बहुत पसंद हैं।
आपको डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए।
examples.translation: You should go to the doctor.

sections.title: Compound verbs (जाना, लेना, देना) & सकना
sections.text: Hindi often pairs a verb stem with a second verb that adds a nuance; the second verb carries the tense. Compounds with लेना and देना are very common in requests and finished actions. With **सकना** and **चुकना** the subject takes no ने even in the past.

examples.text: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?

sections.title: Negation & question words
sections.text: **नहीं** goes just before the verb; in the present the final है is usually dropped: **मैं नहीं जाता** (I don't go). A tag **न?** at the end asks for agreement, like "isn't it?".

sections.title: Summary: building a sentence

examples.text: कल मैंने अपने दोस्तों के साथ एक अच्छी फ़िल्म देखी।
examples.translation: Yesterday I watched a good film with my friends.

examples.text: अगर आपको समय मिले, तो ज़रूर आइए।
examples.translation: If you get the time, do come.

points: Verb last; postpositions after the noun, which takes its oblique form (कमरे में, लड़कों को).
Gender everywhere: adjectives in -आ, का/के/की and most verb forms agree.
Tenses: करता है (habitually), कर रहा है (now), किया (did; ने + object agreement), करेगा (will).
Politeness: आप with plural verbs and -इए requests (बैठिए, कीजिए).
'To me' constructions with को: मुझे पसंद है, मुझे चाहिए, मुझे करना है.
